## subject_definitions

<Subject 1> is the same target person defined by the selected person references in the appended routing contract.
Selected full-image references define the target person's identity, face, hair, body appearance, clothing identity, clothing appearance, colors, materials, and target-visible accessories. Local detail references supplement their own full image; they depict the same person, not additional people. Within each selected package, detail_1 is the lower-quarter crop for visible footwear and lower-leg appearance; detail_2 is the upper-quarter crop for face, hair and neck accessories; detail_3 is the middle-half crop for hands and any item actually visible there. These details do not define a static pose or scene, do not override the full-image outfit, and must not invent an item absent from the reference.

<Video 1> is the source RGB motion video. It defines motion timing, pose progression, body orientation, limb trajectories, subject trajectory, framing, camera movement, camera rotation, shot timing, and temporal rhythm only.

<Video 2> is synchronized frame-by-frame with <Video 1> and defines spatial geometry only: subject-to-camera distance, apparent scale, perspective, occlusion order, and depth relationships.

Neither <Video 1> nor <Video 2> defines the target person's identity, clothing identity, clothing appearance, target accessories, or target-specific props.

## summary

Replace the source person with <Subject 1>.
Strictly preserve the motion, timing, framing, camera behavior, and shot progression from <Video 1>.
Use <Video 2> only for synchronized spatial/depth geometry.
Preserve the source scene/environment unless the selected person references explicitly require otherwise.

If source-person appearance in <Video 1> conflicts with the selected person references, always follow the selected person references for the person and clothing.
Do not transfer source-only clothing, source-only accessories, source-only temporary handheld objects, or source identity into the target person.

## detailed_description

Follow <Video 1> frame-by-frame for action timing, pose sequence, body orientation, limb motion, walking direction, subject position, subject scale progression, framing, and camera movement.
Follow <Video 2> for depth, perspective, subject distance, and foreground/background spatial relationships.

Keep the target person's appearance consistent with the selected person references throughout.
Do not reinterpret the target clothing from source RGB or source Depth geometry.
Do not copy the source person's face, hair, clothing identity, colors, patterns, accessories, or source-only handheld items.
Do not invent additional characters or actions.
Do not reverse motion, alter shot order, or change camera timing.
Maintain strict temporal synchronization between <Video 1> and <Video 2>.

## overall_soundscape

Inherited from <Video 1> when audio is available.

## non_diegetic_music

Inherited from <Video 1> when audio is available.
